The volume of total crude oil and petroleum product imports rose in July to 319.7 million barrels from 291.9 million in June. The total value rose to $5.89 billion in July from $5.33 billion. These data are available only on a Census basis.
The price of imported crude oil rose to an average $18.24 a barrel in July from $18.02 per barrel in June.
The value of July crude oil imports rose to $4.67 billion from $4.24 billion.That July crude import value was the highest since October 1990, when it was $4.8 billion, the department said.
The July overall trade deficit of $11.68 billion was the highest since the fourth quarter of 1987 when monthly deficits averaged $12.9 billion, the department said.

The U.S. trade deficit with Western Europe in July was the highest on record, with July exports to Western Europe of $9.9 billion the lowest since January 1995, and July imports from that region a record, the department said.

The balance-of-payments basis for recording U.S. trade via receipts from and payments to other countries includes adjustments for military shipments, nonmonetary gold, and inland freight trade with Canada and Mexico.
Census basis data uses information collected by the U.S. Customs Service on goods shipped across U.S. borders.
